summary: Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He has served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and held the Edmund J. and Louise W. Kahn Endowed Chair at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2026).

Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, later holding posts at Oberlin College (attested 2013) and visiting positions at Academia Sinica and Dharma Drum Buddhist College.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where his doctoral supervisors were Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1797 to 1801. He subsequently served at Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 until 1852.

Justus Olshausen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, later serving as professor at Kiel University (1823) and Chief Librarian and Professor of Oriental Languages at Königsberg (1852).

Jyotirindranath Tagore was an Indian scholar who worked in Indology and other fields. He received his education at the Hindu School and Presidency College, Kolkata, studying at the latter from circa 1864 to 1867.

János Szerb worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University (circa 1974–1980), he became a research associate and lecturer at the University of Vienna in 1982 and a Buddhist studies researcher at the ISTB in 1986.
Jérôme Ducor specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May from circa 1978 to 1992, and held a position at the University of Lausanne from circa 1996 to 2020.

Józef Kowalewski worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vilnius and Kazan universities, he headed Mongol studies and became rector at Kazan Federal University (1833–1860) before serving as professor and dean at the University of Warsaw from 1862.
Józef Turczyński held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music from circa 1915 to 1919 and the Chopin University of Music from circa 1920 to 1939, where he taught Constantin Regamey.

József Budenz was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, where he completed his doctorate in 1858 under Theodor Benfey. He later served as librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and full professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

Jörg Heimbel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD at the University of Hamburg (completed 2014) and studying at Tibet University, he held posts at Hamburg, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (circa 1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, subsequently serving there as Associate Professor from circa 2007 to 2023.

Jürgen Hanneder specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and Alexis Sanderson, later working as an assistant at Halle-Wittenberg (circa 2000–2007) and becoming a professor at Marburg in 2007.

Jürgen Renn is a historian of science who earned his PhD from TU Berlin in 1987. He served as Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994) and became Director of the MPI of Geoanthropology in 2022.

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He succeeded Sakkottai Krishnaswami Aiyangar in 1929 and held posts at Annamalai University (circa 1930–1947) and Mysore University (circa 1952–1956).

K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist who taught D. N. Shukla. He served as Professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972 and 1987) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer worked in the field of Indology. He served as the Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and as Secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).
K. Jayakumar is an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School in Thiruvananthapuram. He served in the Indian Administrative Service from circa 1978 to 2012.
